source_snapshot.procedure: Use dd-created files to fill all available storage until full, hash the files, reboot once and verify the hashes again; collect results and inspect logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Files fill the spaces without errors and retain correct MD5 values after reboot.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes that arbitrary storage must not be filled but its generic write check does not cover persistence across reboot.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Preserves the fill/hash/reboot intent while prohibiting raw-device or automatically discovered target selection.
historical_reviews.related_cases: This is a filesystem-capacity and persistence test, not a raw-device endurance or performance workload.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Every generated byte must remain inside an approved mount and every cleanup action must be bounded by a recorded file manifest.

original_test_intent: Verify that each approved test filesystem accepts generated files through the specified full or near-full boundary without I/O error and that those exact files retain their hashes after a controlled reboot.
original_method: After explicit target and destructive-scope approval, the agent writes uniquely named tracked files within each approved dedicated mount, monitors free space and health, records hashes, performs one authorized reboot, verifies boot/remount and hashes, then removes only manifested test artifacts as directed.
manual_activity: User approves exact mounts, fullness limits, data loss boundary, reboot and cleanup; operator confirms backup and recovery readiness; agent manages only approved files and evidence.
required_inputs: Stable approved mount/volume/filesystem list and explicit system/storage exclusions
Exact full versus near-full threshold, metadata reserve and stop margin
Generated-file size/count/pattern, hash algorithm and manifest location
Workload quiesce, backup, cleanup and data-recovery owner
One-reboot plan, remount expectations, OOB/console and boot recovery
safety_requirements: Resolve each target to a mounted approved filesystem and never write a raw block device
Exclude OS, boot, EFI, swap, production, RAID-member and unknown storage unless individually authorized
Monitor capacity, metadata/inodes, RAID/NVMe health, latency, temperature and service impact
Preserve pre-existing logs and stop on ENOSPC outside the expected boundary, I/O error, read-only remount, health event, boot failure or hash mismatch
Delete only files listed in the run's immutable manifest and never auto-repair or repeat reboot
agent_execution_scope: Capture storage identity, capacity, inode, mount, RAID and health baseline
Create and hash only manifested test files while enforcing approved reserve and abort thresholds
Perform one approved reboot and verify boot, remount, file count and hashes
Clean only authorized test artifacts; do not select targets, repair filesystems, delete unrelated data or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Own OOB, boot, filesystem/RAID and backup recovery decisions
Review fill, hash, reboot and cleanup evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A bounded file fill is directionally useful, but a generic user-selected percentage and write check omit the source's all-target scope, complete manifest/hash comparison and reboot/remount checkpoint.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Within each explicitly approved dedicated mount, generate uniquely named files to the approved reserve, record per-file hashes and full capacity/health output, reboot once, remount and compare the complete manifest before approved cleanup.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: File-based fill, pre/post-reboot hash validation, one reboot and the source 15/8 timing fields are preserved; actual execution needs an approved safety threshold.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a guarded per-mount file manifest and reserve threshold, with continuous filesystem/storage health monitoring and an auditable single reboot boundary.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Constrains dangerous 'all available storage until full' wording to approved filesystems and adds deterministic cleanup, recovery and complete persistence evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No source target is silently removed; any unsafe system volume must be explicitly excluded or separately authorized rather than auto-filled.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Space exhaustion can break metadata allocation and services before nominal zero free bytes; the approved platform-specific stop boundary governs execution.

project_override_considerations: Thin provisioning, snapshots, quotas, compression, RAID rebuild reserve and container overlay filesystems can make apparent free space misleading; the approved capacity model must identify the backing allocation domain.
expected_evidence: Stable volume, mount, filesystem, capacity, inode, RAID and SSD identities
Timestamped fill progress, free-space/metadata state and all command exit statuses
Immutable generated-file manifest with hashes before and after reboot
Authorized cleanup, restored free space/health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master procedure and Criteria consistently require file fill and post-reboot integrity; DeepSeek narrows execution for safety but its missing coverage is a review deficiency rather than an ambiguity in the original source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Exact targets, threshold and recovery are high-risk execution approvals, not an irreducible semantic blocker; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Transforms an unbounded capacity-exhaustion instruction into traceable per-filesystem file generation, immutable hashes, one reboot and manifest-bounded cleanup without claiming a hardware result.
independent_technical_reasoning: A filesystem can fail before reported free blocks reach zero because metadata, reserved blocks, quotas or thin-pool capacity exhaust first. Hash persistence also depends on completed writes, remount and the exact file set, so a generic near-full write is insufficient; target identity, reserve policy, sync state, immutable manifest and post-boot comparison are all required.
